name: Cory Booker

items.text: In a February 2012 radio interview, Mayor Booker said Newark's unemployment rate fell 2 points in the past year. His office backed this with real federal data comparing January to December 2011, which were not seasonally adjusted. PolitiFact rated it False because the December-to-December drop was 0.7 points. His office called the statement accurate.
items.why: This is a disputed way of presenting his record as mayor (criterion 6), but the figures were real and nothing shows he meant to deceive.

for_review: The owner-sites search (Booker plus alexjoneslive.com, stewpeters.com, ryandawson.org, infowars.com) returned nothing relevant to this item. I read only the PolitiFact ruling, not the original WBGO interview or the BLS tables. The verdict is context because the figures were real and nothing shows intent to deceive. A reviewer who treats a PolitiFact 'False' as enough for criterion 6 could make it a weight-1 'against' instead. Attendance (40 of 915 missed, well under the 100-vote line) raised no concern. I looked for no other items.
